# Round54 mineral frontier: catapleiite

Recorded at 2026-10-12T10:39:55Z. Curator: codex (GPT-6; codex). Trusted base: `5c83f27fa4d916a8432894e07031c2b5c7451a09`.

Admit [catapleiite](../../../data/records/catapleiite.yaml) as one mineral species with bounded natural-specimen and processed-material context. The choice follows the elpidite source frontier. No optional microbial mechanism, criticality or recovery yield is supplied without evidence. Existing elpidite and yusupovite files are untouched. This source investigation is not an independent scientific approval.

## Identity and accepted evidence

The retained September 2026 IMA-CNMNC original was re-inspected at definitions page 1, Catapleiite page 38 and Calciocatapleiite page 35. Catapleiite is `Na2Zr(Si3O9)(H2O)2`, grandfathered (G), year 1850, Norway. The year is not an approval accession. Calciocatapleiite is a separate accepted species. The original was acquired in prior round53 and reused with the identical SHA-256 recorded below; this round does not claim a new live IMA download. The live official one-page Handbook entry was downloaded and viewed; its monoclinic description is not transferred to every natural specimen. The mineral, elemental zirconium, elpidite, mixed rock and experimentally altered derivatives remain separate concepts.

[Cegiełka et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.24425/agp.2022.140427) was obtained through a new University of Warsaw institutional route. The file has one repository cover and the complete 11-page published article, pages235–245. All12 rendered pages, seven original figures and six tables were personally inspected. The cover lists a reversed author sequence, but the published article byline and citation establish Cegiełka as first author; the record follows the article. The repository inventory reports877812 bytes, whereas the delivered PDF is1611902 bytes including its cover; both receipts and actual checksum are retained without silently equating them.

The loose Dyrnaes River block was attributed by the authors to the Ilímaussaq Green Granite using colour and mineralogy. Methods on236–237 describe electron microprobe work; Figure3B, Figure6 and Table5 identify catapleiite in zircon-bearing aggregates with elpidite. This is the same natural specimen and study already represented under elpidite, not a new independent experiment or pure mineral feed. No sample-specific diffraction is shown in that study. Formation, later sodium loss and the reaction to elpidite are geological interpretations. The record does not convert them into controlled microbial or chemical-reaction measurements.

[Zubkova et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.3390/min10030243) was acquired as the complete ten-page publisher PDF and XML from MDPI's public resource host after its main website returned403. All ten original pages, three figures and five tables were personally inspected. The host route was prospectively constructed and then verified by the downloaded document's DOI, title, author list, publisher imprint and Crossref metadata; it was not originally obtained from a successfully opened publisher landing page. No challenge or authentication was bypassed. The acquired XML contains zero supplementary-material nodes and no supplement links; the PDF has no supplementary section. A speculative s001.zip candidate returned404, which alone is not proof that no supplement ever existed.

The2020 material subjected to silver exchange was an annealed zirconosilicate obtained by heating catapleiite at1000°C, not hydrated unheated catapleiite. Figure1a and1b reuse earlier structural models (thesis2012 and thermal study2019); the new structure determination concerns the silver-exchanged derivative. Its0.05g/5mL1M AgNO3,250°C,30day assay and five electron-microprobe spots belong to this laboratory derivative. Na below detection is not zero, five spots are not five independently replicated batches, and no dissolved-metal balance or isolated recovery yield is established. The record retains only this boundary context, not a mineral-level exchange mechanism or numerical performance claim.

## Source conflicts and limits

- In2022 Figure3C the printed label is SZR while the caption calls it catapleiite. Figures3B/6 and Table5 separately support the bounded author-assigned occurrence. No particular polymorph is inferred from a map.
- Table4 and Table6 repeat IL-356 under different material headings. These are not independent phase confirmations.
- Page240 says Na2O spans2.36–14.17wt%, while Table5 includes15.32 and14.35wt%. Table5 also displays cation totals outside the abstract's shorthand interval. The record flags the sodium discrepancy and imports neither dataset ranges nor alteration percentages.
- The2022 analytical appendix and Supplementary Table1 are still unacquired. The newly inspected institutional ORIGINAL bundle has exactly one bitstream (the main article) over one page of inventory. This narrows that route's availability; it is not a claim of universal supplement absence. Previous blocked PGl/PAS routes were not retried unchanged.
- The2020 paper reports poor crystal quality after thermal/exchange treatment and limited anisotropic refinement. Ca was excluded from structural refinement despite being measured by microprobe; Table2 states the distinction. Section3.3 mentions assumed minorNa incorporation despite Methods reportingNa below detection. These do not support numerical natural-mineral exchange claims.

## Bounded follow-ups and acquisition deferrals

The author-uploaded [Yakubovich2013 primary](https://doi.org/10.1134/S1063774513030280), also cited in the IMA row, was available as full indexed11-page PDF text. Direct author-PDF download returned403; web screenshot returned no image block. The public MSU author page was acquired after decoding its declared cp1251 encoding, but contains only the citation, no original file link. Original figures/tables were therefore not visually checked and its specimen measurements are deferred. Its natural orthorhombic structural study is a useful next identity refinement, not an accepted new dataset here.

A new source lead, “Recovery of Catapleiite and Eudialyte from Non-Magnetic Fraction of Eudialyte ore Processing of Norra Kärr Deposit”, has an institutional locator `https://publications.rwth-aachen.de/record/840880/files/840880.pdf`. Direct HTTP200 returned a248-byte HTML interstitial, despite the `.pdf` suffix; that artifact is explicitly not a PDF and its recovery measurements are not curated. Acquire full primary methods, original graphics and feed mineralogy before considering a separate ore-fraction owner or mineral-specific claim. No microbial mechanism lead with adequate primary evidence emerged from the bounded catapleiite query; returned generic bioleaching papers do not establish such a mechanism.

The yusupovite CIF query forAM-15-75092 did not provide an inspectable original in the returned set. Its prior complete main-paper record remains unchanged. The monazite2023 lead is already represented by the existing mixed-feed record and no new owner was justified from its citation alone. The new source searches are not an exhaustive mineral inventory.

## De-duplication and provenance

Cycle-safe traversal included hidden and ignored files and followed symlinks in `data`, `research`, `reviews`, `history` of both current worktree and original checkout, then181 existing referenced raw roots. It read4152 corpus text files and7747 total unique text files. Nine referenced roots were missing and ten files exceeded16MB; unextracted binary files were not semantically searched. The full receipt lists every boundary. Hits were existing elpidite/yusupovite context, IMA inventories and prior research; no maintained catapleiite owner or2020 accepted experiment was found within this declared boundary. The shared2022 experiment is expressly reused rather than called novel.

Bounded DOI/title notice queries and acquired Crossref2020 relation/update metadata identified no affecting notice in returned evidence. No assurance of exhaustive corrections coverage is implied. Bulk sources remain outside Git at `/private/tmp/cmm-round54-mineral-frontier-research`. The pairedJSON records acquisition URLs, actual UTC/statuses, exact retained raw hashes and inspection coverage. The file initially named `zubkova2020.html` was verified XML and renamed to `zubkova2020.xml`; the acquisition receipt preserves the original transient filename. The false `.pdf` response from RWTH remains labelled as non-evidence in this dossier.

## Validation and review handoff

Actual named validation passed: one record checked, zero failed. The exact published-base baseline is reused under the parent initialization receipt; no new baseline run is claimed by this agent. Parent owns final corpus/history/site/review gates and publication. Record/history are frozen for an independent reviewer; no passing review is claimed here.
